note: Written in our own words from clinical knowledge and free instruments (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5 themes). Not DSM text. Draft for clinician review. ADHD and substance use are 'consider' conditions: symptom overlap only, no neurodevelopmental content. Eating disorders are also a 'consider' condition, added from concepts in Ali's earlier ED work (functional analysis: the same behavior can serve different purposes). ED entries carry no numbers (weights, calories, sizes) by design.

symptoms.label: excessive worry about many everyday things
variants: constant worrying about work, health and family

symptoms.label: worry that is hard to control
waking very early and unable to get back to sleep
unwanted memories of a traumatic event
variants: memories of the accident pop up

symptoms.label: nightmares about a traumatic event
variants: wakes from nightmares of the crash

symptoms.label: flashbacks, feeling the event is happening again
strong distress or body reaction at reminders of the event
variants: heart pounds near the place it happened

symptoms.label: avoiding reminders of a traumatic event
variants: avoids the street where it happened

symptoms.label: being constantly on guard for danger
using alcohol or drugs to cope
unwanted thoughts of causing harm that feel alien
variants: scared she might hurt someone though she doesn't want to
horrified by thoughts of harming the baby

symptoms.label: need for order, symmetry or things feeling just right
variants: redoes things until they feel right

symptoms.label: mental rituals such as counting or repeating phrases
variants: repeats a phrase to cancel bad thoughts

symptoms.label: rituals that take more than an hour a day
variants: late to work because of rituals

symptoms.label: urges or rituals that are hard to stop
trouble keeping attention since childhood
variants: teachers said he never paid attention

symptoms.label: using more or longer than intended
withdrawal symptoms when stopping
variants: shaky in the morning until he drinks
sweats and nausea when not using

symptoms.label: asking for reassurance again and again
variants: keeps asking if everything will be okay
asks the same question and it only helps for a minute

symptoms.label: rigid food rules or eating rituals
variants: has to eat foods in a certain order
cuts food into tiny pieces before eating
rules about which foods are allowed

symptoms.label: restricting food out of fear of gaining weight
variants: skips meals so she won't gain weight

symptoms.label: repeatedly checking body shape or size
variants: checks how clothes fit many times a day
keeps pinching his stomach to see if it changed

symptoms.label: exercise that feels driven or compulsory
variants: has to earn food by exercising
guilty if she skips a workout, even when sick

symptoms.label: avoiding foods out of fear of choking, vomiting or textures
variants: only eats soft foods for fear of choking
won't eat anything new since getting sick

concentration.adhd: long-standing, across settings, not tied to mood or worry

irritability.ptsd: tied to reminders and being on guard

numbing.substance_use: ask which came first; do symptoms persist when sober?

intrusive_thoughts.ocd: felt as senseless, followed by rituals

urges_rituals.ocd: done to lower dread, not enjoyed
urges_rituals._note: ask what the ritual is about: contamination, harm or order points to OCD; food, weight or body points to an eating disorder

reassurance_seeking.ocd: about harm, locks or things feeling right
reassurance_seeking.eating_disorder: about food amount, weight or body
reassurance_seeking._note: wording alone does not settle it: ask what the asking does for the person and whether it is speeding up over time

food_rituals.ocd: done to prevent harm or make things feel right, not about weight
food_rituals.eating_disorder: tied to weight, shape or control of eating; ask if the rule is about the body
